audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer sides read Skill on rows 0, 1 and 2 while the content layer and packet levelChart all read Orianna.
audit.why: 50.1% over 962 games. The first three levels are Orianna's on reach — Command: Attack is 815 against Death's Hand at 750, and Nevermove is a 12-second cooldown he cannot spam. From level 4 the root-and-pull all-in arrives and the lane is even until two items.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side set to Orianna with all three whys rewritten in the same group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why claimed your level 6 doubles your lane presence; the row is Skill and the actual level 6 event is his.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, drains health from nearby champions and minions at 650 range, and lasts indefinitely while he keeps draining champions — that is what flattens your poke advantage at 6, and it is why the row is Skill rather than yours.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and breakdown.spikes rewritten around the flat 120-second drain that outlasts chip damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never says how Nevermove actually works, and treats Demonic Ascension as the lane's timer when it is not.
audit.why: Nevermove (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, 850) launches forward and roots on the RETURN trip, after which he can pull every rooted champion toward him — so the dodge is about where you stand when it comes back, not when it is thrown, and its cooldown is shorter during Demonic Ascension. Vision of Empire (W, 22/21/20/19/18) reaches 5500 units at rank 1 and 7500 at rank 5, slows, reveals, and feeds him a Soul Fragment off any champion it hits, which is why a frozen wave on his side is dangerous from off-screen. Ravenous Flock (P) converts those fragments into healing and permanent maximum health.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, winCon and the do/don't bodies now carry the return-trip root, the 12-second cooldown, the 5500-unit W and the flat 120-second ultimate.
sources: enemyKit E/W/P/R text, cooldowns and ranges

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no number and pointed at the wrong ability as the lane's clock.
audit.why: Nevermove at 12s rank 1 is what gates every step forward in lane; the ultimate is a fight-level timer, not a step-up one.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Nevermove's 12s, Death's Hand's 7s and the flat 120s ultimate.

audit.why: report[8].t already says to add anti-heal early into his sustain, and Ravenous Flock explicitly heals him off Soul Fragments, so that advice stands and I left it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions feed asks for a 'bypasses stacking resistances — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer' line off a percentHealth flag on Ravenous Flock.
audit.why: Riot's text for Ravenous Flock says the fragments heal him and permanently increase his maximum health. That is health gain on his side, not percent-health damage on yours, and nothing in the kit says his damage ignores resistances. Flag misfire — not written.
audit.corrected: Not written. Only the healing and the permanent health gain are stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles. suspectNames flagged "Demonic Ascension's" in whys[4].
audit.why: The flagged string is an ordinary possessive of the correct ability name — a false positive, left alone.
audit.corrected: Both bled bullets rewritten to match their titles; the name flag ignored.

The page's biggest gap was Nevermove: it roots on the RETURN trip and he can then pull every rooted champion, and none of that appeared anywhere — the page instead named Demonic Ascension as the lane's clock, which is a fight timer rather than a step-up timer.
